newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were inactive, with light bids of $66.00 per cwt passed by owners pricing cattle $68.00 to $69.00, feedlot sources said.

Fed cattle prices were expected to be underpinned by smaller supplies of cattle on showlists in some areas, compared with last week and outlooks for continued active beef demand as the outdoor cooking season approaches, sources said.
Beef demand is traditionally strong following Easter as retailers promote more outdoor grilling cuts, Dave Maher, analyst with Securities Corp of Iowa, said.
"The whole key is to watch what the wholesale market does," Maher said.

Afternoon beef prices were quoted down $0.61 to up $0.03 per cwt on 169 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported. Beef movement last week totaled 1,344 loads of fabricated cuts, well above 838 the previous week, USDA statistics showed.

The Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area showlist was estimated at 90,000 head, down 5,000 from last week, sources said. The showlist in Kansas was pegged near 85,500 head, about unchanged. Nebraska's showlist was estimated near 80,000 head, steady with last week.
